hints: Find the weight component acting down plane BC for Q ($0.6g \sin 30^\circ = 3\text{ N}$) and down plane AB for P ($0.3g(0.4) = 1.2\text{ N}$).
Since $3\text{ N} > 1.2\text{ N}$, Q accelerates down plane BC and P accelerates up plane AB.
Form Newton's second law equations: $3 - T = 0.6a$ for Q and $T - 1.2 = 0.3a$ for P, then solve simultaneously for $a$ and $T$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the component of weight along each plane:
For Q on plane BC: $0.6g \sin 30^\circ = 0.6(10)(0.5) = 3\text{ N}$
For P on plane AB: $0.3g \sin \theta = 0.3(10)(0.4) = 1.2\text{ N}$

Write Newton's second law for particle Q moving down plane BC:
$$0.6g \sin 30^\circ - T = 0.6a \implies 3 - T = 0.6a$$

Write Newton's second law for particle P moving up plane AB:
$$T - 0.3g(0.4) = 0.3a \implies T - 1.2 = 0.3a$$

Add the two equations to solve for acceleration $a$:
$$(3 - T) + (T - 1.2) = 0.6a + 0.3a \implies 1.8 = 0.9a \implies a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find tension $T$:
$$T = 1.2 + 0.3(2) = 1.8\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Consider two particles connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley at B.

Step 1: Determine the direction of motion.
- Downward weight component of Q along BC: $W_{Q,\parallel} = m_Q g \sin 30^\circ = 0.6 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 3\text{ N}$.
- Downward weight component of P along AB: $W_{P,\parallel} = m_P g \sin \theta = 0.3 \times 10 \times 0.4 = 1.2\text{ N}$.
Since $3\text{ N} > 1.2\text{ N}$, particle Q accelerates down plane BC and pulls particle P up plane AB.

Step 2: Set up equations of motion for each particle:
For particle Q ($m_Q = 0.6\text{ kg}$) accelerating down BC:
$$m_Q g \sin 30^\circ - T = m_Q a$$
$$3 - T = 0.6a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$
For particle P ($m_P = 0.3\text{ kg}$) accelerating up AB:
$$T - m_P g \sin \theta = m_P a$$
$$T - 1.2 = 0.3a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Step 3: Solve for acceleration $a$:
Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate $T$:
$$(3 - T) + (T - 1.2) = 0.6a + 0.3a$$
$$1.8 = 0.9a$$
$$a = \frac{1.8}{0.9} = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Step 4: Solve for tension $T$:
Substitute $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into Equation 2:
$$T = 1.2 + 0.3(2) = 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8\text{ N}$$
Check with Equation 1: $T = 3 - 0.6(2) = 3 - 1.2 = 1.8\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.Applying Newton's Second Law: Forms $3 - T = 0.6a$ and $T - 1.2 = 0.3a$, and solves simultaneously to obtain $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $T = 1.8\text{ N}$.

hints: Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy of Q descending $2\text{ m}$ down plane BC: $\Delta PE_Q = 0.6g(2 \sin 30^\circ)$.
Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy of P ascending $2\text{ m}$ up plane AB: $\Delta PE_P = 0.3g(2 \times 0.4)$.
Apply the work-energy principle: Loss in PE of Q - Gain in PE of P - Work against friction = Gain in total kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}(0.3 + 0.6)v^2$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the loss in potential energy of Q moving $2\text{ m}$ down plane BC:
$$\Delta PE_Q = m_Q g(2 \sin 30^\circ) = 0.6 \times 10 \times (2 \times 0.5) = 6\text{ J}$$

Calculate the gain in potential energy of P moving $2\text{ m}$ up plane AB:
$$\Delta PE_P = m_P g(2 \sin \theta) = 0.3 \times 10 \times (2 \times 0.4) = 2.4\text{ J}$$

Set up the work-energy equation with work against friction $W_F = 1.8\text{ J}$:
$$\Delta PE_Q - \Delta PE_P - W_F = \frac{1}{2}(m_P + m_Q)v^2$$
$$6 - 2.4 - 1.8 = \frac{1}{2}(0.3 + 0.6)v^2$$
$$1.8 = \frac{1}{2}(0.9)v^2 = 0.45 v^2$$

Solve for the final speed $v$:
$$v^2 = \frac{1.8}{0.45} = 4 \implies v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Apply the work-energy principle to the connected two-particle system moving from rest through a distance of $s = 2\text{ m}$.

Step 1: Change in gravitational potential energy for each particle:
- Particle Q descends distance $s = 2\text{ m}$ along BC inclined at $30^\circ$. The vertical drop is $h_Q = 2 \sin 30^\circ = 1\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost, Q}} = m_Q g h_Q = 0.6 \times 10 \times 1 = 6\text{ J}$$
- Particle P ascends distance $s = 2\text{ m}$ along AB inclined with $\sin \theta = 0.4$. The vertical rise is $h_P = 2 \sin \theta = 2(0.4) = 0.8\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{gained, P}} = m_P g h_P = 0.3 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 2.4\text{ J}$$

Step 2: Work done against friction:
The work done against the frictional force along plane BC is given as $W_F = 1.8\text{ J}$.

Step 3: Total kinetic energy of the system:
Both particles start from rest and move with common speed $v$:
$$KE_{\text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}m_P v^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_Q v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(m_P + m_Q)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.3 + 0.6)v^2 = 0.45v^2$$

Step 4: Form the work-energy equation:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost, Q}} - \Delta PE_{\text{gained, P}} - W_F = KE_{\text{final}}$$
$$6 - 2.4 - 1.8 = 0.45v^2$$
$$1.8 = 0.45v^2$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work-Energy Principle: Evaluates PE changes $6\text{ J}$ and $2.4\text{ J}$, forms work-energy equation $6 - 2.4 - 1.8 = 0.5(0.9)v^2$, and evaluates speed $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
